[PERSISTENT EXPERIENCE GUIDANCE]
## Consolidated Experience from Similar Tasks
The collected process experiences consistently show that manipulation actions fail unless the robot first navigates to the target object and verifies it is within reach. A pick-up attempt should never be made from a distance, because the robot cannot grasp an object that is not near it. Similarly, a place action should only be attempted after confirming that the robot is actually holding the object; if it is not holding anything, the pick-up action must be performed first. The general principle is: for each object, locate it, navigate to it, verify proximity/reachability, pick it up, then navigate to the destination, and only then place it. Always check preconditions before acting, and recover by navigating or picking when the precondition is not met.

## Preliminary Thinking
1. Locate the plate. 2. Navigate to the plate and verify it is within reach. 3. Pick up the plate, confirming the gripper is holding it. 4. Navigate to the black table. 5. Verify the robot is still holding the plate, then place it on the black table. 6. Repeat the same sequence for the screwdriver: locate, navigate, verify reachability, pick, navigate to black table, verify holding, place. 7. Repeat the same sequence for the cleanser: locate, navigate, verify reachability, pick, navigate to black table, verify holding, place. 8. If any pick-up fails because the object is not near, navigate closer and retry. If any place action is attempted and the robot is not holding the object, return to the object, pick it up, and then place it.
[/PERSISTENT EXPERIENCE GUIDANCE]
